accepted_gaps.title: Function-versus-universality gap
accepted_gaps.statement: Evidence for homochirality in terrestrial biochemistry is often rhetorically promoted to a universal requirement for all possible life without a defined reference class.

accepted_gaps.title: Scale-bridging gap
accepted_gaps.statement: Prebiotic enantioenrichment, polymer replication, molecular folding, and Darwinian evolvability are frequently studied separately; their evidentiary links are not consistently represented.

accepted_gaps.title: Alternative-architecture gap
accepted_gaps.statement: Cross-chiral and mirror-compatible systems demonstrate alternatives to a single shared convention, but their implications for viable life-like systems have not been formalized as a constrained comparison.

accepted_gaps.title: Definition-sensitive inference gap
accepted_gaps.statement: Claims that chirality defines life lack a preregistered mapping from a chosen life definition to measurable chemical capabilities.

rejected_overclaims: A single prebiotic mechanism is known to have caused terrestrial homochirality.
A cross-chiral ribozyme is a mirror organism.
Existing evidence proves that achiral life is impossible.
